name: bottom-sheet-aria
title: Bottom Sheet (React Aria)
description: A bottom sheet on the native dialog: it follows the finger, settles on snap points with a velocity-aware spring, dismisses on a flick, and grows from its content before the list scrolls.
author: Cory Schulz (Magic Spells) <https://github.com/magic-spells>
docs:
Installed the Bottom Sheet in `components/bottom-sheet/`: `bottom-sheet.tsx` (the parts), the gesture and snap code it runs (`sheet-controller.ts`, `drag-gesture.ts`, `snap-points.ts`, `spring.ts`), its dialog layer and its stylesheet (`bottom-sheet-styles.tsx`, rendered by the sheet itself), plus `--bottom-sheet-*` color tokens for light and dark.

First, give it a trigger, a title and some content:

```tsx
import {
  BottomSheet,
  BottomSheetClose,
  BottomSheetContent,
  BottomSheetDialog,
  BottomSheetHeader,
  BottomSheetTitle,
  BottomSheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/bottom-sheet/bottom-sheet"

<BottomSheet snapPoints={[40, 70, 100]}>
  <BottomSheetTrigger>Open</BottomSheetTrigger>
  <BottomSheetDialog>
    <BottomSheetHeader>
      <BottomSheetTitle>Details</BottomSheetTitle>
      <BottomSheetClose aria-label="Close">×</BottomSheetClose>
    </BottomSheetHeader>
    <BottomSheetContent>…</BottomSheetContent>
  </BottomSheetDialog>
</BottomSheet>
```

- The header (and an optional `BottomSheetFooter`) is always a drag surface; the content scrolls, and a downward drag at the top of its scroll moves the sheet. With snap points, an upward drag on the content grows the sheet before the list scrolls.
- `snapPoints` are percentages of the viewport height; a flick steps one snap, a slow drag lands on the nearest, and dragging below the shortest dismisses. `useBottomSheet().snapTo(70)` moves it from code.
- Restyle it with the `--bottom-sheet-*` properties (colors, radius, handle, padding, durations, `--bottom-sheet-panel-max-width`); its rules are unlayered, as upstream's are, so a utility like `[--bottom-sheet-panel-max-width:36rem]` works where `max-w-*` does not.
- The default (no primitive) variant uses the native `<dialog>`; the Radix, Base UI and React Aria variants keep the same API on those dialogs.
- Reduced motion: no slide, no settle travel; drags still follow the finger.
